 1 / 6 The ultimate Black Friday beauty shopping guide
 Black Friday has a unique ability to tempt even the most serious skincare fanatic to rethink their position regarding their skincare wishlist. However, before the sale notifications turn into an embarrassing collection of products, it’s time to ask a more meaningful question: What products are really worth having? The answer lies in knowing how to separate the great deals from those that should not be included in your skincare products. So, how do you make this kind of purchase? Let’s find out.
 2 / 6 Broad-spectrum sunscreens: The everyday essential worth stocking up on
 If any skincare product should take priority during a beauty sale, it should be sunscreen. Unlike a mask or a complex treatment serum, sunscreen is something you need daily and requires constant replenishment. A broad-spectrum sunscreen with an SPF of 30 or more is ideal. If you plan to spend a lot of time outdoors, look for one with water-resistant properties and a texture comfortable enough to apply generously and reapply multiple times.

 3 / 6 Gentle cleansers: The underrated beauty purchase
 The fact that cleansers are often ignored when it comes to beauty sales is due to their lack of the glamour that luxury serums or popular treatments have. However, they are among the products you will surely make use of often. When it comes to a mild cleanser, the product must remove dirt, excessive sebum, sunscreen, and makeup without making your skin feel excessively tight and uncomfortable.
 (Image Credits: Pinterest)
 4 / 6 Makeup staples you already know work
 The Black Friday shopping season is also a great time to replenish makeup items you’ve tried and enjoyed in the past. Now think about everyday items like foundations, concealers, eyeliners, lipsticks, and mascaras. If you have discovered a certain shade and formulation that works well, buying it again at discounted prices is an easy decision. You might want to invest in quality brushes, sponges, and cleaning products. Nevertheless, be certain to purchase them from authorised outlets and confirm that they have not been opened or used before buying.
 (Image Credits: Pinterest)
 5 / 6 Haircare essentials: Shampoos, conditioners, and treatments
 When it comes to purchasing, hair products are a good choice. This is particularly true if you already have an existing hair care routine. You can proceed to replacing the hair products you already have at home, which include shampoos, conditioners, leave-in conditioners, and heat protectors. If your hair has undergone chemical treatments, is coloured, or is regularly heat-styled, you can choose suitable products.
 (Image Credits: Pinterest)
 6 / 6 What should you avoid now?
 The viral skincare gadgets that make big promises: Recently, skincare gadgets have become popular with shoppers. They are facial cleansing brushes, microcurrent devices, LED masks, and many other beauty gadgets usable at home. However, not all the devices in the limelight have enough clinical evidence to back up their claims. The evidence quality varies from one gadget to another.
Complicated skincare kits with multiple active ingredients: A skincare set that includes the cleanser, toner, exfoliating serum, retinol, vitamin C, and other treatment products might seem like a wonderful bargain. However, getting a bunch of active ingredients without clear insight into their interaction can complicate the skincare process immeasurably. For example, using several products containing exfoliating agents or powerful active ingredients simultaneously can lead to more skin irritation, dryness, and sensitivity.
